Baseline comparison

Model assumptions, limitations, and validation

Steady, incompressible flow; uniform bulk mean velocities; one kinetic-energy correction factor α at both sections; pump losses represented by shaft-to-hydraulic efficiency; gravitational acceleration 9.81 m/s². Elevation difference is z₂−z₁. A positive hydraulic head is required for pumping. Negative or greater-than-100% inferred pump efficiency indicates that the specified operating point is inconsistent with the assumed pump model. This is an operating-point energy balance, not a manufacturer pump curve, system curve, cavitation model, or transient simulation. No viscosity, friction-factor, NPSH, or affinity-law prediction is included.

Reference case: Q = 0.1 m³/s, ρ = 860 kg/m³, D₁ = 0.08 m, D₂ = 0.12 m, ΔP = 250 kPa, Pₑ = 25 kW, ηₘ = 90%, α = 1.05, Δz = 0. Expected: v₁ ≈ 19.8944 m/s, v₂ ≈ 8.8419 m/s, h ≈ 12.6354 m, Pₕ ≈ 10.66 kW, Pₛ = 22.5 kW, ηₚ ≈ 47.38%. The simulator performs an automatic reference regression test at startup.
